text.text_excerpt: Seems like this place gets mixed reviews, but I'll share my experience. Saturday for lunch, was in the area, walked by and we decided to stop in. Very friendly and fast service. Fresh warm chips and two types of salsa were brought out. I was partial to the green one, thought it was different in a good way. I had a beer and my friend had a house margarita, which she said she really liked. Ordered the chicken quesadilla, which is no frills, but tasty. The steak nachos were also ordered and were quite good. Overall, we enjoyed Panchita's. The service was good and the food would satisfy if you had a hankering for simple Mexican cuisine.

This is my new favorite Mexican restaurant in New Orleans...I have passed by so many times, and never managed to go in. Well, I'm glad I did. First, the free chips and salsa are amazing (why doesn't everyone do that??) There is a homemade green and red..So fresh and yummy, lots of cilantro - love it! If it's your first time heading over - try the sampler platter, it's big enough for two and you get to try a little bit of everything. After going back several times - I have fallen head over heels for their empanadas. I like to try out their different homemade sauces too, and last time they brought out the chipotle sauce for a topper. Delish! Be sure to order a big old Mexican Coke to compli...

Being from southern california, I have had my fair share of good mexican food and this is by far the best place I have been in New Orleans. Ive tried a lot of different places around the city and really nothing compares to panchitas on taste and price. Their giant $30 plate is incredibly awesome and delicious and you will leave stuffed beyond belief (ive always shared it with one other person). Lesser people might bring home leftover but if youre a trooper its amazing. also good left over though. Would def recommend.
